newsitem.title: ITALY: Depression caused Lancia matricide, says lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Depression caused Lancia matricide, says lawyer.

text.p: Mental illness led the granddaughter of the founder of the Lancia car company to stab her mother to death at the family's villa, her defence lawyer said on Saturday.
"There is no other explanation than (mental) illness," Cesare Zacconi, defence lawyer for Giovanna Anna Maria Boglione, told reporters in this northern city.
"I believe magistrates will immediately order a (psychological) examination," he added.
Turin magistrates were to question Boglione in hospital later on Saturday, judicial sources said.

Boglione, 44, was taken in a state of shock to hospital on Friday where she was being held under guard after her mother, Eleonara Maria Lancia, was found dead at the luxury villa in the hills outside Italy's car capital Turin.

Lancia was one of three children of Vincenzo Lancia, a former test driver for Fiat who founded his company in 1906. He died in 1937 and control of the firm passed to his wife and former secretary, Adele.
Italian newspapers said Boglione had stabbed her mother in the heart as she lay in bed on Friday night after celebrating her 70th birthday with relatives and friends.
""Mamma', take this knife to the heart," ran a headline in Turin's La Stampa daily.
It said Boglione had been suffering from depression after recently separating from her husband, adding that her mother had invited her to stay a few days at the villa to relax.

The Lancia name became a byword for luxury and racing cars and produced the sleek black Astura Lungo limousine which Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini had built especially for a visit to Italy in 1938 by Nazi Fuehrer Adolf Hitler.
The company sold a majority stake to the Pesenti financial group during hard times in 1955 and was on the verge of bankruptcy in 1969 when it was taken over by Fiat.
